answer: The copper graph is validated at intake and the beacon frontier is published, and hence the ancestry of every answer is public, and dawn anchors the chain at a checkpoint. A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 32 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. Honest users pay that once, farms 10 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
